Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2606.09118v3. Rubric calibration/data construction and publicbenchmark versus companiontraining scope establish substantive methods. Prior Corecraft findings are connected studies, not fresh replications. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The instruction-following result is one training seed, and the authors have not quantified seed-to-seed variance. They describe causal isolation of rubric-design choices and transfer mechanisms as future work; comparisons with other pipelines use different base models/training setups and are suggestive rather than controlled.

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Domain experts draft prompts/reference responses and rubrics; a second expert reviews and a senior reviewer adjudicates disagreements. Calibration compares hand judgments with an LLM verifier and response edits designed to flip verdicts.
  • GPT-5-mini supplies per-criterion training judgments. The instruction-following reward is the fraction of required criteria satisfied, rather than wholly deterministic code verification.

  • The instruction-following result uses one training seed without quantified seed variance. Cross-pipeline comparisons differ in base models and training setups; controlled transfer-mechanism/design isolation remains future work.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ComplexConstraints describes a three-stage expert prompt/reference/rubric authoring and independent-review workflow, plus iterative LLM-judge calibration and response edits designed to flip verdicts. Qwen3-4B training uses about 900 of the 1000 companion prompts, with GPT5-mini judging required criteria; the 75-prompt public benchmark is separate.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Table 3 reports Qwen3-4B mean per-criterion pass rate increasing from 57.9% to 73.4% on the held-out ComplexConstraints training split. This criterion-average metric differs from the all-criteria task pass rates on the separate 75-prompt public benchmark.
